newsitem.title: POLAND: PEPSICO UNIT VICE-HEAD EYES E.EUROPE GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: PEPSICO UNIT VICE-HEAD EYES E.EUROPE GROWTH.

text.p: PepsiCo's restaurant unit plans to lift its number of outlets in Poland from 49 to 170 in the next three to five years, the restaurant division's president for Central Europe said on Monday.
Peter Maslen told a news briefing that PepsiCo's late-January decision to spin off its restaurant business should help units of the new company gain investment capital.

"It (PepsiCo's separation) gives us faster access to capital and resources...rather than having to stand beside my beverage colleagues...I really only have to compete with the other restaurant companies," Maslen said.
PepsiCo Inc plans to spin off its restaurant businesses, including KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell, to PepsiCo shareholders as an independent publicly-traded company.
Maslen said his company had already invested $57 million in Poland since 1993, with employment, currently at 3,000, likely to rise to 10,000 in three to five years.

Maslen said Poland was the region's most promising market not only because of its 40-million population, rapid economic growth and literate workforce, but also because of the entrepeneurial nature of the people.
John Wells, CEO of Wedel, majority-owned by Pepsico, said that despite rumours he had no knowledge of a plan by the parent company to either increase or decrease its share in the confectioner.
